title: Observability — Live Matrix (system pulse, real-time)
description: The 'watch the system run' dashboard. 5-second refresh, dense layout, real-time event streams, live histograms, top-N rankings. Designed to be left up on a wall in a NOC — the shape of what you see tells you whether the system is bored, busy, or burning. Tighter time window and faster refresh than the other dashboards on purpose; this one is for *now*, not history.

panels.title: Live event streams — what's happening right now
Kernel (warn+) — live tail
panels.description: Kernel ring buffer, severity warn+. Refreshes every 5s. The shape of message bursts tells you whether the kernel is under stress.

panels.title: ZFS dbgmsg — live tail
panels.description: ZFS internal debug ring buffer (`/proc/spl/kstat/zfs/dbgmsg`). Scrub start/end, resilver progress, TRIM activity, vdev events, snapshot create/destroy — all surface here.

panels.title: Container + pod events — live tail
panels.description: Container runtime + pod lifecycle events (kubelet, containerd, conmon). Pod creates / deletes / probe failures appear here.

panels.title: Anything error-level (all sources) — live tail
panels.description: Catch-all: anything emitting at err+ across the journal. The 'what's on fire right now' panel.

panels.title: Distributions — heatmaps refreshing in real time
Block read latency (kernel block layer)
panels.description: Read latency distribution from the kernel block layer (BPF kprobe on `block_rq_*`). Hot band moving up = something is getting slower. Tail thickening = outliers appearing.

panels.title: Tetragon event handling latency (kernel → userspace)
panels.description: How long Tetragon takes to handle each kernel event end-to-end. Hot top = userspace is falling behind the kernel.

panels.title: Hottest BPF programs by CPU time/s
panels.description: Top 10 Tetragon BPF programs by kernel CPU time/sec. Tells you which observability hook is the most expensive RIGHT NOW.

panels.title: Loudest kernel syslog identifiers (msgs/s)
panels.description: Who's talking on the kernel ring buffer right now. Outliers = something noisy. Pair with the live kernel tail to read what it's actually saying.

panels.title: Cilium BPF maps closest to eviction
panels.description: Top 10 BPF maps by fullness ratio. Anything > 0.8 = sizing problem brewing. Sustained 1.0 = active evictions = lost connection state.

panels.title: Network — Hubble flows + TCP flags + drops
Hubble flows/s (1s rate)
panels.description: Every TCP/UDP/ICMP flow between pods, observed in-kernel by Cilium's eBPF data plane. No sidecars, no agents, no app cooperation.

panels.title: TCP flags rate (SYN/RST/FIN/ACK)
panels.description: Connection lifecycle visibility. SYN bursts = new connection storms. RST = aborts (interesting). FIN = clean closes.

panels.title: Tetragon events by msg_op (live, stacked)
panels.description: msg_op 13=EXECVE (process exec), 14=EXIT (process death), 15=KPROBE (policy-defined kernel probe), 16=TRACEPOINT. EXECVE bursts = something just spawned a lot of processes.

options.content:
### How to read this dashboard

- **Pulse row** is your one-glance read. Every panel has a sparkline behind the value — the shape tells you trend at a glance. If everything is flat-green, the system is bored. If any panel is yellow/red, look up.
- **Live event streams** refresh every 5s. They scroll like a syslog terminal. Reading them is reading the system's stream-of-consciousness.
- **Heatmaps** show distribution shape. Hot bands moving up = things slowing down. Tail thickening = outliers appearing. A clean heatmap with a narrow band = healthy.
- **Top-N bar gauges** show who's most active *right now* (1-minute window). Use them to find the noisy actor when something looks off in the pulse row.
- **Network row** is Hubble's eBPF view of every flow. No sidecars, no Envoy, no per-app agents. The kernel sees every packet.

### What unlocks when we ship more eBPF data

- **Process exec stream as live tail** — needs Tetragon → fluent-bit → Loki shipping (the JSON export pipeline). Once wired, replaces the 'container + pod events' tail with literal `execve` lines: `[t] pod=X comm=python3 args=foo.py exit=0 dur=1.2s`. That's the Splunk-can't-do-this moment in flesh.
- **Scheduler runqueue + softirq heatmaps** — needs `runqlat` + `softirqs` ebpf_exporter configs added. Adds two more heatmap tiles to the distribution row.
- **TCP RTT + lifetime heatmaps** — needs `tcprtt` + `tcplife` configs. Adds the per-connection forensics tier.
- **Off-CPU flame graph (Pyroscope)** — needs Pyroscope deployed. Adds the 'where threads are blocked' answer eBPF is uniquely able to give.
